questions.q: What determines the actual table name once a @dlt.table pipeline runs?
options: The comment parameter passed to the decorator
It's always named the same as the file it's defined in
You must explicitly specify a separate name parameter every time
The Python function's name — bronze_trips becomes the table bronze_trips
questions.explain: The decorator declares metadata; the function name itself becomes the table's real name.

questions.q: What does the function's return value represent in a @dlt.table definition?
options: A string describing the table's purpose
A boolean indicating whether the table succeeded
The DataFrame that Lakeflow materializes as that table's actual contents
The table's schema definition only, not its data
questions.explain: This is exactly the DataFrame this course has built with the same PySpark methods all along.

questions.q: Why would you use @dlt.view instead of @dlt.table for an intermediate step?
options: It participates in the same dependency graph but is never materialized as its own queryable Delta table, avoiding clutter in the catalog
@dlt.view runs faster than @dlt.table in every case
@dlt.view cannot use dlt.read() to reference other steps
@dlt.view is required before any @dlt.table can be defined
questions.explain: Useful for breaking a long transformation into named, readable pieces without adding tables nobody needs to query directly.

questions.q: How do table_properties in a @dlt.table decorator compare to Lesson 40's approach?
options: They live in the same place as the table's transformation logic, in one self-contained function, rather than a separate CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE statement
They have no equivalent to anything covered in Lesson 40
table_properties cannot be set for a @dlt.table at all
They require running a completely separate SQL script after the pipeline
questions.explain: This is a real structural difference — one function versus separate statements.

questions.q: What does the comment parameter in a @dlt.table decorator do?
options: It's purely a Python code comment with no effect on the pipeline
It determines which schema the table is created in
It sets the retention window for VACUUM
Provides a description shown in the catalog, similar to metadata associated with a table
questions.explain: This mirrors the kind of table-level metadata Lesson 40's catalog/schema setup also deals with.
